edit.description: peek_and_validate_seam_version (~1905): a payload that does not parse, or carries no version, reports as PayloadParse; only a read version that differs is a seam mismatch
the tests[] line's test, end to end: a non-JSON SDK payload refuses as a payload parse error. It lives here, never as a drift.rs unit test, which would carry the fix to the base run.

summary: peek_and_validate_seam_version maps any JSON parse failure to UnsupportedSeamVersion { got: 0 }, so a non-JSON program stdout is misreported as SDK/engine version skew
acceptance: a non-JSON or version-less payload refuses naming the parse failure, and a mismatched version still refuses as a seam-version mismatch
tests: a payload that is not JSON refuses as a payload parse error, not a seam version mismatch
notes: Scenario: a stray console.log in harness.ts puts a second line on stdout and emit says "payload declares seam version 0". The three existing peek tests (drift.rs ~7680) cover only well-formed JSON.
